question: For $x>0$, determine the critical point of $f(x)=x+\frac{4}{x}$. Examine the sign of $f'(x)$ on either side of this point.
explanation:
First derivative
$$f'(x)=1-\frac{4}{x^2}=\frac{x^2-4}{x^2}$$
Critical-point condition
For $x>0$, set $f'(x)=0$:
$$x^2-4=0\Rightarrow x=2$$
The value $x=-2$ is rejected because it is outside the given domain.
Sign to the left
For $00$, so $f'(x)<0$.
Sign to the right
For $x>2$, $x^2-4>0$, so $f'(x)>0$.
Conclusion
The only critical point in the domain occurs at $x=2$. The derivative changes from negative to positive there.
